title: Thinner Agents on a Smarter Substrate: The Ontology-based Semantic Layer — Emil Eifrem, Neo4j
talk_summary: Emil Eifrem argues that scaling many agents requires 'thin agents on a smarter shared substrate': a business-facing ontology, a technical ontology of data sources, and runtime execution traces that let agents learn which sources work. The mechanism is centralizing intent-to-data mapping and success signals in a shared graph instead of re-wiring each agent's code and prompts.

takeaways.what_they_do: Agents record where they were, what they tried, and whether it succeeded, producing a score that biases future source/tool selection, shared across agents rather than per-agent.
takeaways.evidence_quote: they leave the third pillar, the execution traces for that... I've been very successful using the DMV lookup... I'm more likely to choose one

takeaways.technique: Business ontology as shared prompt substrate
takeaways.what_they_do: Key domain concepts and their relations are defined once in human-readable terms and referenced by all agents, instead of each agent's prompts re-describing the domain.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you don't say if underscore name. No, you have a customer and they have a first name

takeaways.technique: Technical ontology mapping intent to concrete sources
takeaways.what_they_do: A maintained map from business concept to system-of-record (e.g. 'first name' -> Oracle column F_name) so agents resolve data/tools without per-agent wiring.
takeaways.evidence_quote: that first name has a system of record and over there there's an Oracle database with a column called F_name

takeaways.what_they_do: Teams that tried to solve shared-context problems with only Markdown files found it partial; the mapping and learning need structure beyond prose.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we've seen a ton of team that tried to solve this problem using just Markdown files... it is part of the solution, but it is not the solution

takeaways.what_they_do: Move repeated wiring and knowledge out of each agent into a shared layer so adding agents doesn't require re-engineering existing ones.
